items.title: Find members in chat by call sign
items.summary: Every member has a chat account before they open chat, and a member who allows being found by call sign carries it after their name, so a chat search finds them by call sign. Radio bridges now work only on a room the member made themselves.

items.title: Element X sign-in
items.summary: Make the newer Element X phone app able to sign in with a site account. It needs the Matrix Authentication Service (native OIDC) in front of the chat server; until then the Chat page points phones to the Element Classic app.

items.title: Code scanning review and fixes
items.summary: Every alert from the GitHub code scanning of the public repository was triaged: real ones fixed (address check, track parser, server-drawn two-factor QR code, restore column checks, exact name matching, input limits), the rest dismissed with a reason.

items.title: Linking islanded mesh areas
items.summary: Two mesh communities with no radio path between them can share one channel: the site carries its packets between their topics (still encrypted), with hop, duplicate and rate limits, agreement by both communities and an administrator's approval.

items.title: Airline schedules for My Flights
items.summary: Look up the scheduled times, terminals and aircraft of a flight number and date from AeroDataBox to fill your diary. Built; it switches on when the site's administrator adds a key.

items.title: Browser notifications for every alert
items.summary: One Notifications page with a switch for every kind: chat, friends, communities, aircraft alerts, mesh nodes, shared flight links, weather warnings, earthquakes, rivers, satellite passes and landed balloons for your places, and items needing attention for administrators.

items.title: Sharing My Flights
items.summary: Share one flight or your whole diary with a link, choosing what shows, and switch it off again at any time.

items.title: Real flight tracks on the My Flights map
items.summary: The Flight Map will draw each flight's recorded track (when it has one) instead of a straight line.

items.title: Matrix chat with Element
items.summary: Chat and direct messages are on a Matrix server of our own with end-to-end encryption, signed in with your ArkSignal account, in the site's own pages and in the Element phone app, with notifications (also when the site is closed), moderation, friends and blocks, and a bridge for amateur radio and Discord. Built and tested; ships with the next release. Calls (they need a relay server) and moving old conversations are not planned yet.

items.title: Admin side menu
items.summary: The Admin section has the same left side menu as My Account.

items.title: Air ambulances on the Trauma Map
items.summary: A single switch on the Trauma Map draws every air ambulance helicopter and airplane the network hears, with a details card.

items.title: Kiosk display
items.summary: A wall-screen mode (Display menu, /kiosk): chosen pages full screen whose menus and map controls hide after a set time with no input and return with any input, an Exit button, a Setup panel (pages, seconds for each, presets, one page only), the date and time at a chosen corner and size, and ?kiosk=1 on any page.

items.title: Space weather
items.summary: Radio > Space Weather: NOAA storm scales, K index, solar flux, flare class and a rough HF band guide.

items.title: Weather overview
items.summary: The Weather overview shows the whole weather setup at a glance: stations, alerts, radar and satellite, earthquakes, rivers, space weather and balloons, with the station map and list below.

items.title: Earthquakes layer
items.summary: Recent earthquakes in and around Arkansas (the New Madrid zone) from the USGS, drawn by magnitude on the maps, with the time, depth and USGS link on click.

items.title: Phone maps: folding top panel and clear popups
items.summary: On a phone the map's top panel folds to one row of buttons once the map is moved, and popups open clear of the panels; the radiosonde Heard By table has a Sort by choice. Floating buttons no longer cover an open card. The Radiosonde Map shows claimed stations as claimed. My Account pages use the site's folding sections. Admin pages all use folding sections.

items.title: Usage history, pickers and filters
items.summary: Admin > Usage keeps request and feed counts by the hour and for all time, with From, To and All Time pickers and filters for the table; a service restart loses nothing.

items.title: One merged map
items.summary: Every map is one page built from one shell, and the Map selector switches the kind of map in place, keeping the view; each type shows only its own layers and filters. We keep it this way rather than putting every filter on one map.

items.title: Smoother wind streams
items.summary: Wind streams follow a smooth blended wind field and curve with it at every zoom. Wind from a forecast model would improve them further.

items.title: Radio overview, repeater position picker and call sign links
items.summary: A Radio overview page, a repeater list with locations, a map picker to set a repeater's position, and links that work for any call sign.

items.title: Service status checked in the background
items.summary: The status page opens at once and shows the result of checks that run on a schedule; only an administrator can force a run.

items.title: Frequencies list
items.summary: APRS, calling frequencies, FRS, GMRS, MURS, weather radio, marine and mesh frequencies in one list.

items.title: Clearer feeder icons
items.summary: Feeders show as airplane badges that can be seen at state level, on the Feeders page and the Coverage Map.

items.title: County Map outline-only look
items.summary: A look that draws just the thin county lines, the same as the County outlines box on other maps.

items.title: Grafana statistics dashboards
items.summary: Weather and radiosonde statistics in Grafana with filters, delivered by the normal update.

items.title: Call signs, contacts and talkgroups
items.summary: One page to look up a call sign, find a DMR contact and browse talkgroups; call sign details show wherever a call sign appears.

items.title: DMR time slots and talkgroups on repeaters
items.summary: Each DMR repeater shows its color code, ID and both time slots with their talkgroups; editors add them from the standard list.

items.title: Weather map for any region
items.summary: The weather map loads only what is in view, anywhere we have data, and never lets labels overlap.

items.title: Radiosonde station coverage from real flights
items.summary: Each receiving station's coverage outline is built from the flights it really heard, like an ADS-B station's.

items.title: Labels that never overlap on every map
items.summary: Aircraft, weather, APRS, repeater, radiosonde and county map labels never overlap; one shared label engine measures every label as drawn and keeps the most important.

items.title: Repeater code plug formats and a review queue
items.summary: More radio export formats and a queue for imported repeaters waiting for a position.

items.title: Weather for any place
items.summary: Type a ZIP code, city, airport or address and get a full weather page made from the stations near it, with the National Weather Service forecast and history charts.

items.title: Drive times from anywhere on a map
items.summary: Click the map to pick a place, or search a city or an address, and the nearest hospitals are listed by road drive time and distance (near-ties by trauma level, then services). Drive-time rings of 15, 30, 60 and 90 minutes can be shown for any hospital or place, on the County Map and the other maps. An estimate from the network's own routing server.

items.title: One list of location precision
items.summary: Twelve steps from exact to hidden, the same on every form and setting, written in your own units. Radiosonde stations show to about 0.7 mile until their owner chooses.

items.title: Highways map layer and hospital drive-time rings
items.summary: Interstates, US and state highways as a map layer on every map, and 15, 30 and 60 minute drive-time rings on hospital pages (an estimate from the network's own routing server).

items.title: APRS stations and weather
items.summary: Digipeaters, gateways, weather stations (CWOP included) and optionally moving stations from the APRS-IS network around Arkansas, with a map, station pages, an APRS weather page and a takedown list.

items.title: Repeater directory
items.summary: Amateur radio repeaters in every mode from Hearham's open data and Arkansas hams, with a map, reports, sysop claims and member submissions. More layers, coverage estimates and extra sources are still to come.

items.title: Phone-friendly pages
items.summary: Menu, section bars, tables as cards, folded map panels and smoother scrolling on phones.

items.title: Balloon landing forecasts and archive history
items.summary: A separate prediction service imports SondeHub's open archive and forecasts where the balloons of upcoming launches will land, then scores itself against the real flights. Members can also load any flight by serial.

items.title: Arkansas trauma list and hospital capabilities
items.summary: Load the state's designated trauma centres and what each hospital can do from the state's own files, with their source shown.

items.title: Interesting aircraft list
items.summary: Keep your own list of interesting aircraft (military, government, rare, news) that feeds the Interesting filter on the map.

items.title: Collapse the map panels from the bottom
items.summary: A small arrow at the bottom of the Filters and Weather panels folds them away.

items.title: Tidier admin area
items.summary: One consistent width for every admin section, the admin area using the full screen width, and shorter, better grouped settings.

items.title: Site icon
items.summary: A signal-arc icon for the browser tab, bookmarks and phone home screens.

items.title: Complete How to Feed pages
items.summary: ADS-B, MLAT and UAT each have their settings, hardware and setup, in the same layout.

items.title: Better hospital positions
items.summary: Hospitals are placed more exactly, with a locate button and the trauma list's own coordinates.

items.title: Automatic data updates
items.summary: One schedule page for every outside data set (places, airports, hospitals, trauma levels, air ambulances), with run now, last result and failures on Status.

items.title: Fixed-wing air ambulances
items.summary: Medical transport aircraft as a second filter beside the helicopters.

items.title: County map
items.summary: A clickable county map: every Arkansas county is one shape, shaded by how many feeders, weather stations, hospitals, airports or balloon launch sites it has, with a page for each county and county layers on the aircraft and home maps. Released in 1.0.31. Later: drive-time rings around hospitals and interstates.

items.title: APRS
items.summary: Amateur radio position reports on the map: stations, digipeaters, IGates and weather, with an APRS coverage map.

items.title: Sign in with Google
items.summary: Members link a Google account on My Account > Google Sign-In and sign in with it (the site checks Google's signed answer itself; accounts are linked by Google's account number, never by email alone; two-factor still applies). An administrator enters the Google client ID and secret to switch it on.

items.title: Passkeys
items.summary: Sign in with a passkey (fingerprint, face, screen lock or security key): added on My Account, used from the sign-in page, checked in full on the server; administrators can remove a member's passkeys.

items.title: Administrators can edit a user's account
items.summary: Open any account to change its profile, email, display choices, alerts and sign-ins; the password is never shown.

items.title: Map legend
items.summary: A collapsible legend that explains whatever the map is showing.

items.title: Trauma level import
items.summary: Load trauma-centre designations from a list and show them on each hospital.

items.title: Air ambulance filter
items.summary: See air ambulance helicopters on the live map and filter to them.

items.title: Hospitals and heliports
items.summary: A hospital list and map layer with emergency care, trauma level and the heliport each one uses.

items.title: Search the map by place
items.summary: Jump to a city, ZIP code or county from the live map's search box; the start of places, hospitals and heliports with drill-down.

items.title: New home page and Aircraft Tracking
items.summary: An ArkSignal overview with a live strip, map preview, one search box and a card per service; the old home page becomes Aircraft Tracking.

items.title: ArkSignal
items.summary: The project has a new name, wordmark and tagline; the same network, now with room for weather, radio and mesh.

items.title: Choose your landing page
items.summary: Pick where you land after signing in, with a site default.

items.title: Coverage Map
items.summary: A map of what the network covers, with layers by type; repeaters, weather stations, radiosondes and mesh nodes join later.

items.title: How to Feed split into pages
items.summary: ADS-B, MLAT, UAT and Am I Feeding each get their own page with a sub-menu.

items.title: Search and sort on lists
items.summary: Search the admin and public station lists; sort Flights, Flight History and Airports by any column.

items.title: Settings tabs and search
items.summary: Admin settings are grouped into tabs, with a search that finds a setting by name.

items.title: Navigation always in view
items.summary: The top menu and a slim bottom bar stay on screen while you scroll long pages.

items.title: Planefence and Plane-Alert
items.summary: Which aircraft flew over Arkansas, with photos, airlines and routes, plus a list of interesting aircraft (military, government, rare). Notifications to Discord and others are set up by an administrator.

items.title: Off-site backups
items.summary: Encrypted copies of everything (database, settings, statistics, traffic history) sent to a server, bucket or NAS elsewhere, a small daily copy and a big weekly copy.

items.title: Restore part of a backup
items.summary: Bring back one area (accounts, stations, flight history...) or a single person, station or alert rule instead of everything.

items.title: Aircraft type filter
items.summary: Show only helicopters, jets, turboprops, piston props, large and heavy aircraft, gliders, drones or ground vehicles.

items.title: Collapsible filter sections
items.summary: Every group of map filters folds up like the aircraft details, remembers how you left it, and shows how many filters are active.

items.title: Keyboard shortcuts popup
items.summary: The shortcuts help opens in the middle of the screen, on top of everything.

items.title: Sign-up checklist
items.summary: Registration and password forms list the requirements and tick them as you type, including whether the two passwords match.

items.title: Live Release Notes and Roadmap
items.summary: These two pages update themselves from the project's repository, so they stay current while work is under way.

items.title: Map revamp: one map for every kind of data
items.summary: Every map shares one layout, icons, popups and settings, with saved views, one search box that never filters, satellite and hybrid styles, your location, county outlines and drive times on every map. The single merged map (one page, lazy modules) is still to do.

items.title: Places, roads, counties and hospitals
items.summary: Counties, county pages, cities, hospitals, heliports, highways and drive-time rings are done.

items.title: Weather stations
items.summary: Members' own weather stations on the weather pages, the weather map and the home page.

items.title: Radiosondes
items.summary: Live balloons, flights, launch sites, receiving stations, recovery reports and chase mode.

items.title: Repeater directory
items.summary: An Arkansas directory of repeaters in every mode (FM, DMR, D-STAR, Fusion, P25 and more) laid out like the airports, started from open data and local lists and kept right by the community. Anyone signed in can submit one or report a correction.

items.title: Meshtastic and MeshCore nodes
items.summary: Where the mesh nodes are, who hears whom, and a guide for joining the Arkansas mesh; every member gets their own broker login on My Mesh Nodes. Still to come: claims, coverage areas and operations help. The overview page shows live numbers, and nodes' Neighbor Info reports draw Direct Links on the map.

items.title: ACARS messages
items.summary: Aircraft datalink messages received by member stations, shown on the aircraft details and on a live messages page.

items.title: Satellite-relayed aircraft
items.summary: Positions of aircraft reported over Inmarsat (JAERO ADS-C), Iridium and HFDL by members' receivers, through the ACARS service: they appear on the live map's ACARS positions layer with the age of the report.

items.title: Support the project
items.summary: A page for donations toward running costs (Ko-fi and PayPal) and an equipment fund for antennas, receivers and mesh nodes the project installs at host sites. The page appears once the project's donation links are set up.

items.title: Native replay and heatmap
items.summary: Replay a past day and see where traffic flies, built into the map instead of the embedded classic tools.

items.title: More of the classic map's features
items.summary: Multi-select, persistence, without-position filter, UTC times, QNH-corrected altitude, auto-select, last flight only, sea-level geometric altitude (EGM96), slim wind labels and the list's show more rows are all built.

items.title: Phone polish
items.summary: The first pass from your phone screenshots is built: full-screen Layers and Filters with an easy Close, a short footer, smaller labels and icons, readable panels and a handful of page fixes.

items.title: Email
items.summary: Password reset by email and alert emails are built, with a test message, on Admin > SMTP: enter a sending service's settings there to turn it on. Account verification by email is not built.

items.title: Admin area allow-list
items.summary: Limit the whole Admin area to chosen addresses and networks (Settings > Security); it cannot be saved from an address that is not on the list, and a server command clears it.

items.title: API keys
items.summary: Members make API keys (My Account) for a documented public API at /api/v1 with per-minute and per-day limits; administrators manage, limit and revoke them.

items.title: Built to scale and survive a failure
items.summary: Designed so the hub, the MLAT server and the portal can run on more than one machine and share the load. Considered as things are built, and done last unless something needs it sooner.

items.title: Weather alerts on the map
items.summary: National Weather Service warnings, watches and advisories drawn as colored areas on the maps (a Weather Alerts layer), with the details on click; the states and refresh are settings.

items.title: River and lake gauges
items.summary: River and lake gauges in and around Arkansas from NOAA's National Water Prediction Service, colored by flood category, with the stage and flow on click.

items.title: River traffic (AIS)
items.summary: Barges, towboats and boats on the Arkansas, White and Mississippi rivers and the lakes from members' AIS receivers: a list, a map, a page for each vessel, a Marine Traffic layer on every map, a How to Feed page with a bridge program, and an administrator takedown list.

items.title: Amateur radio extras
items.summary: Space weather and HF band guide (Radio > Space Weather), net schedules (Radio > Nets) and Winlink gateways (Radio > Winlink Gateways), the last two kept by members with an editors' check.

items.title: Drone Remote ID
items.summary: Drones that broadcast Remote ID, heard by members' own receivers (ESP32 scanners or phones): a list, a map, a page for each drone, a Drones layer on every map and a How to Feed page with a bridge program. The operator's location is not kept unless an administrator allows it, and pilots can ask for an ID to be hidden.

items.title: Satellite imagery and passes
items.summary: Visible and water vapor satellite imagery and lightning layers (Weather panel), and Radio > Satellite Passes: pass predictions for the space station, weather satellites and amateur radio satellites over any place. The Satellites map layer shows where each satellite is now with its path, what it can see and a card on how to work it (frequencies, mode, equipment, Doppler on the pass page). Members' own weather satellite receivers (Meteor-M, GOES, NOAA) send decoded pictures to a gallery (Radio > Satellite Images), each receiver with a private upload address. Weather > GOES Imagery shows NOAA's newest GOES-East and West pictures for the Arkansas region and the country. Satellite receivers have a How to Feed page and an uploader script. GOES Imagery adds full disk views for GOES-East and GOES-West and animation loops; members' satellite pictures are put together into loops the same way. The GOES viewer zooms, picks the loop length and fills the window; the passes page picks satellites with grouped buttons and shows how to work only the one you look up.

items.title: Discord bot
items.summary: Alerts in Discord from a bot of the site (needs Marty to create the Discord application and give the site its token). Kiosk mode is built (its own item).

items.title: Phone app
items.summary: An installable phone app. Its own item, only if it is ever done.

items.title: Messages
items.summary: Email-style private messages between members: Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Archive and Trash, a subject, several recipients, threads with Reply and Reply to All, read and unread, search; administrators cannot read them, moderators see only a reported message.

items.title: Chat
items.summary: Live chat between two or more members: direct chats and small named groups, messages that appear without reloading, typing and seen notices, online dots and unread counts in the menu; moderators see only a reported message.

items.title: Friends lists
items.summary: Send, accept and decline friend requests, see which friends are online, start a chat or a message in one click, block a member, and choose who may contact you (everyone, friends only, nobody new).

items.title: Radio bridges for chats
items.summary: Link a chat to an APRS call sign (messages out from your own call sign, replies in) or to a Meshtastic node. APRS is built and opt in with licensing notes; the mesh side is ready on the portal and waits for the mesh gateway. APRS needs a verified license: the call sign is checked against the FCC amateur license data, re-checked weekly, with administrator review and override.

items.title: Station achievements and leaderboards
items.summary: Badges for feeders (range, uptime, activity, age) on the Feeders page and each feeder's page, with a section that says what each takes and who holds it; the ranking table was already there.

items.title: One-click updates for the whole stack
items.summary: New services appear on the hub with the Update button and no commands: the stack updater, MLAT and the hub itself.

items.title: MLAT
items.summary: A network MLAT server, MLAT status for every station, an MLAT network page showing who is synchronised with whom, and recognition by MLAT user name.

items.title: How an aircraft is tracked
items.summary: The aircraft card says whether a position came from ADS-B, MLAT, UAT/ADS-R, TIS-B or none, and how many stations hear it.

items.title: Service Status pages
items.summary: A plain-words status page for everyone and an in-depth one for administrators.

items.title: A complete How to Feed guide
items.summary: How ADS-B, MLAT and UAT work, setup for new and existing stations, ports, troubleshooting and privacy.

items.title: Classic map features: units, shortcuts, search, filters
items.summary: Units (aeronautical, metric, imperial), keyboard shortcuts, search with lists and wildcards, data source and flags filters, jump to a place, shareable links, altitude chart and KML export.

items.title: Release Notes
items.summary: What was added, improved and fixed in every release, back to the first.

items.title: Easier navigation on every page
items.summary: A grouped top menu (overview first, map second) and an always-visible bar on every page.

items.title: ArkSignal: a new name
items.summary: The network is ArkSignal: new name, wordmark, About page and emails.

items.title: A new home page with a page for each service
items.summary: The overview home page is live with a map of every kind of station and a card for each service, and each service has its own overview page and menu.

items.title: Report and correct repeaters
items.summary: Submit a new repeater, flag a wrong frequency or tone or one that is off the air, and let sysops keep their own current, with a review queue and credit to contributors.

items.title: Address lookup for hospitals and our own address search
items.summary: Look up a hospital's address with the Census, our own Photon and OpenStreetMap, see the answers on a small map and keep the one you choose.

items.title: Check all hospital positions at once
items.summary: One button checks every hospital's address with two address finders, confirms the ones that agree and lists the rest for review.

items.title: Hospital data issues flag and filter
items.summary: Flags hospitals with missing information, doubtful positions or a heliport that is not close to the hospital.

items.title: Collapsible Filters and Weather panels on the live map
items.summary: A small arrow on the bottom edge folds the open panel up so the map shows.

items.title: Altitude bar always visible on the live map
items.summary: Keep the altitude colour bar at the bottom of the map so it can be read at all times.

items.title: Places menu group
items.summary: Move Hospitals and Airports out of the Aircraft menu into their own group for places and facilities.

items.title: Settings regrouped
items.summary: The long Maps and Data Sources settings are split into groups that match what they control.

items.title: One width for every admin section
items.summary: Admin pages use the whole window and every section is the same width.

items.title: Full service status with outside data sources
items.summary: The status page shows every service and every outside data source we depend on, and how fresh our copy of each is.

items.title: A real admin overview
items.summary: What needs attention, the network, the data and the system at a glance, with recent activity.

items.title: Organised admin menu
items.summary: Admin pages are grouped by purpose and kept in a fixed order, enforced by a test.

items.title: Feet and miles by default
items.summary: Distance settings default to imperial units with metric available.

items.title: Map button in the top bar
items.summary: A simple Map button beside Display so the live map is one click from anywhere.

items.title: Full-width pages with one section width
items.summary: The whole site, not only admin, uses the full window width with every section the same width.

items.title: Home page station map and Right Now panel
items.summary: The home map shows every kind of station across Arkansas, and the panel beside it shows what is worth a look right now.

items.title: Page width choice for ultra-wide monitors
items.summary: Page content is limited to a comfortable width by default, with full width one click away, saved on your profile.

items.title: Show on Map links
items.summary: Airport, hospital and weather station pages have a Show on Map button that opens the live map on that place.

items.title: Flight paths that separate
items.summary: A flight that lands out of range and flies again later is drawn as its own path, not joined to the earlier one.

items.title: Home Assistant integration and Tempest bridge
items.summary: Install ArkSignal Weather from HACS, choose your weather device and it sends the readings; Tempest owners without Home Assistant run a small bridge that listens to their hub locally.

items.title: Weather map with layers and filters
items.summary: A full Weather Map with radar and satellite layers, a station list, wind arrows, filters and a details card; the same markers on the live map and the Weather page.

items.title: Home page for Arkansas only
items.summary: The home page's right-now numbers, cards and map count only what is in Arkansas, with a margin at the border.

items.title: Faster Planefence
items.summary: Streamed and compressed data, cached pages and a fence limited to low-flying aircraft, and Plane-Alert can use the Interesting Aircraft list.

items.title: Admin forms to add things for a member
items.summary: Administrators add a weather station, feeder or radiosonde station for a member with every option the member has, finding the member as they type.

items.title: Granular administrator roles
items.summary: Separate permissions for weather stations, radiosondes and map data (and a repeater moderator for later), so someone can be an administrator of one service only.

items.title: One registry for every service
items.summary: A new service appears on the home map, the home Right Now card, the admin Overview, About, the Feed menu and the roles from one place, with a checklist and a test.

items.title: Stations at the same place
items.summary: Feeders, weather stations and balloon stations that share a location fan out on the maps instead of hiding each other.

items.title: Balloon recovery reports and chase mode
items.summary: Signed-in members report recoveries to SondeHub, see recovered, planned and unrecoverable sondes on the map, and use a chase mode.

items.title: Predictions for future balloon flights
items.summary: Where the next launches from each site are likely to land, learned from years of history: a landing area, burst height and flight time, with a score of how well it did before.

items.title: SondeHub archive import
items.summary: Bring in SondeHub's open archive for Arkansas and the surrounding launch sites, as far back as it goes, so predictions start with years of data.

items.title: A prediction and archive service
items.summary: The heavy work runs in its own container with its own database, so it can move to another host as the network grows.

items.title: Read-only production access
items.summary: A locked-down login that lets Claude read logs and container state on the hub, and nothing else.

items.title: Backups kept in step with every feature
items.summary: Every table has a restore area and a test fails when a new one does not.

items.title: Hospital drive-time rings
items.summary: Rings on the map showing how far an ambulance can drive from each hospital in 15, 30 and 60 minutes.

items.title: Send your weather station to the APRS network
items.summary: Owners can send a weather station's newest reading to CWOP or APRS-IS as an APRS weather report (with consent, their own ID or call sign, a preview and a Send Now button).

items.title: Satellite map
items.summary: A satellite imagery base map on every map.

items.title: Your location on every map
items.summary: An option to show where you are on any map.

items.title: APRS and airport weather on the Weather Map
items.summary: The APRS weather stations and airport weather in the same format as the members' stations, without duplicates.

items.title: Live weather layers
items.summary: Heat maps, wind streams, UV and cloud across the state from every weather source and the balloons.

items.title: Statistics with real filters
items.summary: Weather and balloon statistics you can filter by area, ZIP, city, county, station, flight or receiving station, with each data source switchable.

items.title: Repeater details for digital radios
items.summary: Talkgroups, DMR and other IDs, call sign lookups and more import options, built around what a radio's code plug needs.

items.title: Radiosonde map and flight details
items.summary: Click a balloon for the same flyout as every other map; filters and search on the heard-by table; forecasts picked from a launch site with dates, like SondeHub.

items.title: Replay and heat map of past traffic
items.summary: The portal's own Replay (play back any past time at up to 100x) and Heat Map (where aircraft flew in any period) on the live map, read from the hub's history files.

items.title: ACARS and satellite datalink
items.summary: Members' ACARS, VDL2 and HF datalink receivers feed a messages page, station pages and the aircraft card. Satellite receivers (JAERO, Iridium) can use the same bridge.

items.title: Repeater code plug export
items.summary: Repeaters out to a radio: the DM32's channel and talkgroup lists, CHIRP and an RT Systems style file, plus a queue for repeaters waiting for a position.

items.title: Mesh nodes (Meshtastic and MeshCore)
items.summary: Nodes that publish themselves, on a list, a map and node pages, with who hears whom, and links to the local meshes. Each member gets a private login for their node.

items.title: Radiosonde Map forecasts can be cleared; Flights can be filtered by receiving station
items.summary: A Clear Forecast button for a launch forecast, and a Heard by list on the Flights page.

items.title: Full screen maps
items.summary: A Full Screen button on every map.

items.title: Radiosonde stations can send frames directly
items.summary: A claimed station can pass auto_rx's payload summary on to ArkSignal through a small bridge, besides the SondeHub feed.

items.title: Mesh broker certificate renews itself
items.summary: The mesh broker takes its certificate from the site's proxy and follows renewals; the public Meshtastic server can also be read, if switched on.

items.title: Usage page
items.summary: What the site asks of outside services and what each service stores.

items.title: Our own forecast data (GFS)
items.summary: The prediction service reads NOAA's GFS model itself (winds by height and the surface forecast, every six hours, for Arkansas and a wide margin): the balloon predictor flies through our own winds and Weather for a Place has an hour-by-hour model forecast. A separate Tawhiri (our own flight model already exists; the Tawhiri option still calls an outside predictor) and a longer-range model are not built.

items.title: Numbered radiosonde forecasts
items.summary: Forecast flights on the Radiosonde Map are numbered in launch order.

items.title: All My Stations
items.summary: One page showing everything you run, by service, with a count for each.

items.title: Linked repeaters
items.summary: Groups of linked repeaters on the list and as lines on the Repeater Map.

items.title: Site themes and seasonal themes
items.summary: Color schemes you can pick, and seasonal and holiday themes that switch on by date, with their own decorations and map icons (Santa planes at Christmas, pumpkin and skeleton balloons at Halloween).

items.title: Units for each service
items.summary: Radiosondes default to metric like SondeHub; every service has its own unit setting, in the Display menu and in each map's Layers and Filters.

items.title: Trauma Map and trauma regions
items.summary: Arkansas' seven trauma regions and two trauma zones on the County Map and on a new simple Trauma Map (Places menu): trauma centers by level, hospitals near the state line, drive times, pictures and websites.

items.title: County and hospital pages: websites, pictures and a bigger map
items.summary: Each county and hospital page links to its website and shows a picture where the map used to be; the map is larger and sits across the bottom of the page.

items.title: Classic tar1090 map retired
items.summary: The live map has every feature of the embedded tar1090 map, so the Classic Map menu item is gone (old links open the live map).

items.title: Display preferences and saved map views in My Account
items.summary: My Account > Display and Maps holds every choice of the Display menu (theme, units for each service, times, page width, map label and icon sizes, trail options) in folding sections, follows you to every device, and lists your saved map views.

items.title: County Map: limit what is shown by state, county or ZIP
items.summary: The County Map's Show on the Map section has a Limit To filter (state, county or ZIP area) that applies to every choice: hospitals, airports, stations, launch sites and the rest.

items.title: NWS stations on the Weather Map
items.summary: Looked at and not built: the National Weather Service's own data service only gives observations for airport stations, which the Airport weather source already shows; its mesonet and RAWS stations reach us through the APRS (CWOP) source.

items.title: Matrix and the Element app for chat
items.summary: Chat and messages move to Matrix so conversations are end-to-end encrypted, with read receipts, typing notices, reactions and notifications. Element Web, themed and framed to look like the site's own chat, signs members in with their site accounts; the built-in chat is replaced. Next big project; needs a host name for Element and the Matrix server.

items.title: Mesh Channels with QR codes
items.summary: Make a private Meshtastic channel with a random key, then share its QR code and address with members, friends or a chat group.

items.title: Mesh owner alerts
items.summary: Tell a node's owner when a router goes quiet or its battery is low.

items.title: Mesh channels and QR codes
items.summary: A channel configurator for the Meshtastic app: create private channels, share them with members and groups, with a QR code to scan.

items.title: Extend the mesh through our broker
items.summary: Two separate mesh areas (for example Little Rock and Sheridan) can share one channel through the site's broker without loops; built as Linked Areas. Waiting for a test with two real nodes.

items.title: Mesh alert and weather channel
items.summary: A community can carry National Weather Service warnings for its area and a regular weather summary out over its mesh on a channel it chooses, within daily limits, with a log of everything sent.

items.title: Mesh node history and coverage planning
items.summary: Charts of battery, voltage and channel use are on each node page, and Mesh Router Planning suggests where one more router would help the most poorly served nodes (a guess from what was heard, not a terrain prediction). Ships with the next release.

items.title: Mesh Communities
items.summary: A page with its own menu, a drawn area, a map, nodes placed by hand, news and events, channels with QR codes, a team and its own broker topic with plain steps for each local mesh (Little Rock, Northwest Arkansas, Hot Springs and others). Ships with the next release.

items.title: Mesh node telemetry
items.summary: Mesh nodes that share battery, voltage, channel use or sensor readings (temperature, humidity, pressure, wind, rain, light) get charts on their page in the site's own chart style, and Mesh Weather lists every node with sensors. Ships with the next release.

items.title: Scoped roles for communities
items.summary: Roles and permissions that apply inside one community only (Viewer, Node Operator, Editor, Manager, Owner), with invitations. Built for mesh communities; APRS groups and repeater clubs can use the same roles later. Ships with the next release.

items.title: Mesh group self-management
items.summary: A mesh group sets up its own gateway logins, uplinks and downlinks, and sees its own statistics, charts and nodes.

items.title: Remote administration of mesh nodes
items.summary: A community's Manager queues rename, role, channel name, reboot and read commands for its nodes; a small program on the group's own computer, next to a gateway node, carries them out so the node's admin key never reaches the site. Changes wait for approval and everything is logged. The site also watches the Meshtastic firmware and protobuf releases. Ships with the next release.

items.title: Notifications on your phone or computer
items.summary: Chat notifications while the site is open (Element's own) and, from My Account > Community Settings, on a phone or computer when it is closed (the site's own Web Push). Aircraft alerts, mesh node alerts and friend requests can use the same notifications. Built and tested; ships with the next release.

items.title: Share files in chats and messages
items.summary: Pictures, files and voice messages in chat (Matrix), with a size limit you set, private to the conversation, covered by the off-site backup, and removed after a set time if the administrator chooses. Ships with the next release.

items.title: Data retention and thinning
items.summary: Admin > Data Retention shows every store that grows with its size and what happens as it ages, thins old weather readings and removes old chat files on a schedule, with a dry run, Run Now, a run log and audit entries. Ships with the next release. Later: rollups with minimum and maximum, and more stores.

items.title: Mesh owner alerts
items.summary: Owners of mesh nodes hear (email, webhook and a list on My Mesh Nodes) when a router goes quiet or a battery is low, and when it recovers.

items.title: Found on Google
items.summary: A sitemap, robots.txt, descriptions and canonical addresses on public pages, noindex on private ones, and Search Console and Bing verification codes in Settings.

items.title: My Account overview and side menu
items.summary: An Overview page where My Account opens, and one left side menu (a drop-down on phones) in groups: Account, Security, My Stations and Community Settings.

items.title: Community Settings
items.summary: Chat, Messages and Friends are their own Community section; their settings (who can contact you, being found, blocked members) are one page in My Account.

items.title: Private name for the license check
items.summary: Private first and last name on the Profile, kept encrypted and shown to nobody, used to check your amateur license.

items.title: Mesh broker keeps its logins
items.summary: The mesh broker now saves the logins it is given, so nodes are no longer refused after the broker restarts.

items.title: Phone menu scrolls anywhere
items.summary: In the open phone menu, long sections such as Aircraft scroll with the whole menu wherever you swipe.

items.title: Faster Backups page
items.summary: The Admin backups page no longer opens every backup file each time it loads, so it stays fast as backups grow.

items.title: Off-site copy to a NAS over WebDAV with https only
items.summary: Back up to any NAS without opening port 22: WebDAV over https (through your reverse proxy), certificate always checked, plain-language errors in the connection test, and the last successful copy shown. Proven with an automated end-to-end test; the real NAS is for the administrator to try.

items.title: Easy off-site backup to a NAS
items.summary: A NAS choice in Off-Site Copy with step-by-step setup (SFTP, a backup-only user, a protected port or VPN) and a connection test.

items.title: Radio bridge in the profile and in every chat
items.summary: A Verified Amateur badge and call sign on the profile, a new member page, chats and messages, a Radio panel inside every chat to link it to APRS or the mesh, a how-it-works box on the Chat page, and a clearer Radio page in My Account.

items.title: Forward mesh data to the public Meshtastic server
items.summary: A community can choose to have what its gateways send also forwarded to the public Meshtastic server, under its rules. Off until the site and the community turn it on; waiting for a test with one real node.

items.title: End-to-end encryption for chats and messages
items.summary: Encrypted conversations that only the people in them can read, through Matrix and the Element app (decided), with sign-in by the site's own accounts.

items.title: Public source code (AGPL)
items.summary: A public copy of the portal's code under the AGPL on a GitHub organization, published at each release with private infrastructure details left out.

items.title: Mesh broker logins stay in step by themselves
items.summary: The site checks every couple of minutes that the mesh broker holds every member's login and sends any that are missing, so an update or a rebuilt broker never leaves a node refused.

items.title: My Flights diary and flight data exports
items.summary: Downloads, the private diary (detailed times, people, seats), route map with recorded tracks, statistics, CSV, GPX, KML and AirTrail import, export, look-ups, flight pages and sharing by link are built.

items.title: Replay of flights and balloons
items.summary: Play back a recorded aircraft flight (or a whole period) on the live map from Flight History, and recorded balloon flights on the Radiosonde Map from the Balloon Flights list, with speed, pause and a slider. Ships with the next release.
